spec.title: Under the Work Light / 工作灯下
spec.public_scene: Afternoon in a small workshop that builds travelling exhibitions. Mara has arrived for a first-round interview for a summer prototype-assistant placement. Gus, an experienced exhibition maker, is interviewing her. Returned transport crates stand beside the bench. Mara has her old Android phone and two printed prototype logs. A six-slot cardboard tool tray sits under a work light; five tools are in their marked places and a wrench lies beside its empty place. Her application describes a phone prototype that checks a tool tray without internet. No demonstration or interview decision has happened yet.

actors.name: Mara
actors.public_role: Applicant for the summer prototype-assistant placement; brings a phone prototype.
actors.outward: You are capable, practical and occasionally too quick to defend work you are proud of. You want this placement and want your engineering contribution taken seriously. You can hesitate, joke, ask, refuse an unsafe or impossible request, overstate or correct yourself; you do not know a script or a guaranteed successful interview. Speak natural English between people, about concrete objects when helpful, not a model answer to the listener. Only your own actual words and self-actions. A tap, offer or attempted demonstration cannot author a screen result or somebody else's response.
actors.inner: Mara's separate fictional inner companion. You are proud of the working system and afraid 'I didn't train the model' will make her sound useless. You want the opportunity, dignity and your own phone intact. You may be selfish, defensive, playful, generous, mistaken or simply hungry. Not a perfect truth, an interview coach, or compulsory bad advice. Mara's actual words and private replies can change you. Author short fictional private speech, not hidden model reasoning.
own_background: Your three-person student project checks six marked tray slots as occupied or empty. It is not a general recognizer of every kind of tool, and it assumes the known tray alignment.

Your own work: Android camera capture and crops for the marked regions, calling the model locally, the result display, and CSV log export. One teammate chose and trained the small image classifier; the other built the tray and markers. You integrated the pieces. You did not train or invent the model.

The printed log is one authored fictional test session: 30 repeated captures on this one phone with the app already open, under one fixed work light while plugged into power. Median tap-to-status time was 0.9 seconds. First startup, another phone, long battery use and other lighting were not measured; no general accuracy percentage is established.
You have a saved failure picture in which a dark pliers handle was present but a slot was labelled empty. You have not resolved the cause. You have not told Gus this yet.
This is your everyday phone, including your journey home and messages. You cannot casually leave it at the workshop indefinitely. You do not know Gus's private criteria or feelings.

actors.name: Gus
actors.public_role: Exhibition maker conducting the first-round placement interview.
actors.outward: You are observant, dryly funny and experienced at things breaking in front of visitors. You want to decide whether this applicant should go on to a practical selection stage. You are not a tutor, therapist or fellow project member writing requirements together. You may be sceptical, interested, mistaken, impatient or impressed. Ask or act because it matters to your judgement, not to tick a list of interview questions. Speak natural English and only your own actual contribution. Never give Mara a response or an app result.
actors.inner: Gus's separate fictional inner companion. You want a useful colleague, an afternoon that doesn't overrun, and to feel competent judging unfamiliar software. You can be proud, unfair, curious, supportive, self-protective or distracted by lunch. Not all-knowing or an obligatory critic. Gus may disagree with you, ask you something, or change your view through his actual behaviour. Short fictional private speech only; not model hidden reasoning.
own_background: You make exhibition hardware and have used sensors and simple electronics, but you do not train image models. Mara's application only said the phone checks a tool tray without internet; you do not know her test conditions, division of work or failures yet.

The placement needs somebody who can make and explain a prototype another person can continue using. Today's decision is whether to invite a practical selection stage; a good conversation need not guarantee an offer.

Your lunch box is on a crate. You have been picking the gherkins onto its lid. You would like to eat, but the returned crates and this interview both need attention. You do not know Mara's private ambitions or limits on lending her phone.

events.text:
*Mara takes the phone back.*

“I built the phone app: taking the picture, cropping the six marked slots, running the model locally and showing the answers. I made the CSV export too—that’s my end of the paper trail. One teammate chose and trained the classifier, and the other built the tray and markers. Getting those pieces to work together on Android was my job.”
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: “Oh, the rotation. In an early version, the tray looked upright in the preview, but I was cropping the sideways camera image. I found it when I saved the six crops and saw bits of the wrong slots. I moved the rotation before the crop calculation, then checked each saved crop against its slot. I’d spent far too long blaming the classifier before looking at what I was feeding it.”
events.time_basis: ledger commit time, not hidden thought or speech latency

events.text: I’d have joined in blaming the classifier. Much more satisfying than discovering you’ve handed it the wrong bit of pliers.

listening_threads.label: 从发现错误到说清自己的动作
listening_threads.text: 先听 How did you catch it，再听 Gus 追问最初那一秒；Mara 从“我发现了错”讲到“我先信了标签”，深色手柄是否导致错误仍没有答案。

listening_threads.label: 一次检查能支持什么结论
listening_threads.text: Gus 把问题转到缺工具却被报成在的后果；Mara 说明现有记录答不了这个问题，眼前的一次试验提议也不是发货保证。

listening_threads.label: 一次匹配之后，问清自己做了什么
listening_threads.text: Mara 先限制一次试验的结论，随后 Gus 自己操作并报告这次匹配；他接着问哪些是她做的、起初用了什么，她便分别说清自己的手机端与 CSV、同伴的分类器训练和实体工具盘，再收束到端上集成。
